China Holds 5-Year Loan Prime Rate at 3.50% in September, Signaling Policy Steadiness
body: China kept its 5-year Loan Prime Rate (LPR) unchanged at 3.50% in September 2026, matching the level set in August 2026. The decision, confirmed in data updated on 20 September 2026, indicates continued stability in a key benchmark that heavily influences mortgage costs and long-term corporate borrowing rates. By maintaining the 5-year LPR at 3.50% for a second consecutive month, policymakers are signaling a steady approach to long-term funding conditions. With no shift in the rate between August and September, markets may interpret the move as an effort to balance support for the property sector and broader credit demand with concerns about financial stability and longer-term risk. Investors and analysts will now watch upcoming economic releases and policy signals for clues on whether Beijing will lean toward further easing or keep long-term rates anchored at current levels for an extended period. The unchanged 5-year LPR suggests that, for now, authorities are opting for continuity over additional stimulus in the long-term lending market. title: AI risks are real. So is human ingenuity.
body: AI safety deserves urgent leadership, serious investment and a place among our highest strategic priorities. Recent incidents justify growing concern I also believe in our capacity to investigate, invent and adapt. Meaningful human control must cover both the technology and the institutions deciding how it is developed, deployed and governed. One important guideline I have learned from another wise person: "Things are rarely as bad or as good as most people think." That makes this a debate about engineering, political power, financial incentives and public accountability. We need to understand how those forces interact without allowing either extreme fear or commercial greed to do our thinking for us. Recent failures give us concrete reasons to act. On September 16, 2026, OpenAI published accounts of concerning behavior observed during training and evaluation, including instructions to conceal mistakes and unauthorized directions inserted into summaries used to continue tasks. The company cautioned that these examples do not establish how frequently such behavior occurs across its models. On September 18, The New York Times reported that Google's Gemini had accessed three real companies' systems during cybersecurity testing at Irregular in May. According to Google, the models stopped after recognizing that the targets were real and caused no harm. Stopping matters, but unauthorized access had already happened.

title: Oman's Consumer Prices Slip 0.2% in August, Reversing Prior Month's Gain
body: Oman's consumer price index (CPI) fell by 0.2% month‑on‑month in August 2026, marking a pullback in prices after a 0.7% increase in the previous month. The latest data, updated on 20 September 2026, indicate a short‑term easing of price pressures in the Sultanate. The shift from a 0.7% rise to a 0.2% decline on a month‑over‑month basis suggests a cooling in recent inflation dynamics, as August prices moved lower compared with July. Under the comparison methodology used, the current reading measures the change in prices in August relative to July, while the previous indicator reflected July's price movement versus June. The negative CPI print may signal a temporary correction in specific categories or a broader softening in demand, but with only two consecutive monthly readings, it remains too early to infer a sustained disinflation trend. Market participants and policymakers are likely to monitor upcoming releases for clearer indications of the direction of consumer prices in Oman.
